- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates downside; add buffer or adjust downward by 2–5% of recent range.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply decay factor to subsequent forecasts (e.g., 0.85 multiplier for next 3 days).
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change 1–2 days ahead.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–75), model often holds too high; reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until reversion completes.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates volatility in sentiment-driven periods; add 1–2% volatility buffer if sentiment is volatile (±0.50 or above).
